primary_meaning: The final place or state of eternal conscious punishment, torment, and separation from God for the unrighteous after judgment

alternatives.meaning: Annihilation or permanent destruction/cessation of existence of the wicked (conditional immortality) rather than endless conscious torment
Temporary remedial or purgatorial suffering leading ultimately to universal reconciliation and salvation of all
Metaphor for present spiritual death, alienation from God, or the natural consequences of sin experienced in this life rather than a postmortem realm
basis: modern existential and liberal theological readings of judgment imagery

alternatives.meaning: Simply the grave or the general realm of the dead (Sheol/Hades) without any implication of punishment or eternal destiny
basis: Old Testament usage of Sheol (e.g., Psalm 16:10, Ecclesiastes 9:10)

notes: Traditional Christian teaching across Catholic, Orthodox, and most Protestant traditions converges on hell as postmortem divine judgment involving lasting negative destiny for the unrighteous; the precise ontology (literal fire vs. relational separation, duration vs. annihilation) remains contested, but the broad punitive/separative sense is the recognizable primary consensus. Imagery of fire, darkness, and worms is widely treated as symbolic even by those affirming a real final state.
